assignments.brief_reason: Uses aggression/fear and personal attacks as the main removal/decision criteria, matching toxicity/aggression moderation.
Downweights mere insults/cursing in favor of substantive content, consistent with removing low-toxicity/harassing material.
Treats physical violence as a hard deal-breaker while otherwise keeping speech.
Keeps only when arguments lack personal attacks/foul framing; personal attacks drive moderation.
Supports free speech while disliking excessive foulness; this aligns with a speech-allowed baseline with profanity not being disallowed per se.
Focuses on debate worthiness/common ground (low-signal dunking) rather than explicit threat/toxicity removal.
Pair selection based on oppositional contrast is a comparison strategy, not a moderation standard tied to threats/toxicity.
Mentions extremeness and false-claim spreading without explicitly framing as threat/toxicity-based removal in the codebook themes.
Explicitly keeps because there is no promotion of violence or hate, matching the violence/hate exception model.
Allows opinions unless people are 'cussing each other out,' which resembles removing toxic/vulgar personal aggression.
Checks whether the main point is kept vs lost, which is not a moderation/toxicity/threat boundary.
Downweights ad hominem without substance as a cue for influence/acceptance, aligning with removing non-substantive toxic behavior.
Describes weighing both responses with free-speech consequences, but not specifically applying identical moderation criteria across both sides.
Cussing leading to lower perceived intelligence is about handling vulgar/toxic language; closest to toxicity removal standard.
Explicitly scans for threatening/violent content and its impact on dialogue.
States tone is the main influence for judgment; aligns with moderation based on toxic/inflammatory presentation.
Uses a free-speech boundary that removes only when posts are explicitly rude/insulting.
Emphasizes preserving perspectives and constraints on removing only one; not a clear threat/toxicity moderation rule.
Influenced mainly by perceived extremity, without clear mapping to threat/violence/toxicity or profanity rules.
Uses civility/language quality and libel checks as moderation cues, consistent with removing toxic/harassing/inflammatory content.
